paper_title: What Does an Evaluation License? A Commit-Bound Census of Claim-Relative Inference in Inspect Evals

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Evaluation artifacts specify a forward computation: a task, scorer, and reported metric. They do not necessarily license the claim attached to that metric because the historical evidence and alternative semantics needed to replay it may be unbound. We formalize this missing claim-replay layer through a frozen substrate D, a grounded family F, a claim query q, and the resulting identified set. We then census all 124 mechanically eligible Inspect Evals units at a pinned commit. Every unit receives a terminal disposition; 110 stop before deterministic inference because required historical evidence or semantic grounding is unavailable. Where execution closes, exact values, winners, complete orders, and pairwise relations separate by claim resolution and by primary versus review family. The audit therefore returns typed stops, instability witnesses, and stable substructure rather than forcing one evaluator meaning or one robust/not-robust label.

sections.title: ABSTRACT
sections.content: Evaluation artifacts specify forward computation: task, scorer, and reported metric. They do not necessarily license the claim attached to that metric because the historical evidence and alternative semantics needed to replay it may be unbound. We formalize this missing claim-replay layer through frozen substrate D, grounded family F, claim query q, and the resulting identified set. We then census all 124 mechanically eligible Inspect Evals units at pinned commit. Every unit receives terminal disposition; 110 stop before deterministic inference because required historical evidence or semantic grounding is unavailable. Where execution closes, exact values, winners, complete orders, and pairwise relations separate by claim resolution and by primary versus review family. The audit therefore returns typed stops, instability witnesses, and stable substructure rather than forcing one evaluator meaning or one robust/not-robust label. Why this object exists. Evaluation artifacts produce scores; they do not by themselves say whether the attached claim can be replayed, or what remains identified when it cannot be recovered uniquely. Our claim-replay object turns that missing inference layer into an inspectable interface. What the census finds. Across the complete 124-unit frame, 110 units terminate with typed, actionable STOP, not zero score or benchmark-failure label. When (D, F, q) is executable, enumeration is deterministic and recovers primary versus review conclusions, claim-specific witnesses, and the stable pairwise backbone. In the deep audits, winners remain identified even where complete orders do not. This retrospective diagnosis motivates release contract; it does not estimate how many future stops the contract would prevent. INTRODUCTION: THE MISSING INFERENCE LAYER

sections.title:
1
An evaluation artifact answers a forward question: what ran, how outputs were scored, and what
metric was reported. A scientific claim asks a different question: would the value, winner, or
ordering survive other grounded readings of the same historical evaluation? That question needs
one additional object—a claim-replay contract binding the historical observations, the admissible
semantic alternatives, and the claim being queried.
We study that object in the complete mechanically eligible frame of the Inspect Evals reposi-
tory/register at one pinned commit (Inspect Evals Maintainers, 2026). The empirical story has
two steps. First, many units cannot reach claim replay because the necessary historical observations,
judge traces, state, support, or semantic registry are absent. Second, when replay is executable, fine
claims may vary while coarser conclusions remain fixed.
Controlled specification interventions in Appendix L show why the second step matters: even
with observations and predictions fixed, changing an omitted semantic coordinate can change the
evaluation conclusion. The census asks the prior infrastructure question—whether historical releases
preserve enough information to make such claim-relative analysis executable at all.
AgentDojo gives the intuition. Five grounded readings of the same attack outcomes change the
displayed scores. The two primary readings agree on the complete order; review-only readings swap
the two lower systems; Claude 3.5 Sonnet remains the winner throughout. Thus one evaluation can
support an identified winner, a primary identified order, and a review-envelope non-identified order at
the same time. Section 2 makes this claim ladder precise.
sections.content: Contributions. We contribute three linked pieces: 1 (i) claim-relative object (D, F, q) that separates primary conclusions from sensitivity to disputed admission; (ii) complete 124-unit census showing where historical claim replay becomes executable and where it stops; and (iii) an executable audit that distinguishes values, directions, winners, complete orders, and stable pairwise structure. The paper follows Figure 1 from left to right: Section 2 defines the object, Section 3 reports the evidence gate, Section 4 studies completed audits, and Section 5 states the executable contract. Reproducibility artifact entry point. The arXiv ancillary file is claim_replay_public_arxiv_v3_reproduction_R2_20260825.zip. Start at README.md; reviewer/RESULTS.md maps each reported result to its machine-readable record, and verification/verify_supplement.py performs the fail-closed checksum and result-profile checks. The package contains the frozen census summaries, complete-audit records, independent source-table recomputations, and executable contract implementation needed to inspect the claims without local filesystem path.

3.1 FINITE FRAME AND TERMINAL ACCOUNTING
At pinned commit 32b79a2, a predeclared mechanical eligibility predicate yields 124 units from
129 strict-path candidates. Five rule-based exclusions are fully enumerated in Appendix B.1; none
depends on an evaluation outcome.
Every eligible unit receives a terminal record. Fourteen reach deterministic claim analysis and 110
STOP earlier in the chain. Of those stops, 103 belong to the outcome-blind census-review path and
seven to the frozen random draw. In the former, the leading primary codes are evidence-binding
failure (47), missing comparative observations (35), and missing judge traces (9); the remaining
twelve concern endpoint/target typing, missingness, claim selection, or terminal state. A stop is not a
benchmark failure or a zero-valued result. It identifies the first unavailable object and the minimum
artifact that would permit claim replay. Appendix B gives the full taxonomy and accounting.

5 EXECUTABLE AUDIT CONTRACT
The contract has one deliberate human boundary. Human auditors define the claim, endpoint type,
comparable support, candidate origin, and A/D/X admission; prospective audits freeze that ledger
before outcomes. Human semantic decisions end there. The contract never asks automation to
discover the uniquely correct evaluator meaning or certify that the family is complete.

5.1 READER-FACING OUTPUT
The audit reports a ladder rather than one robustness label: value image, direction or threshold,
winner/top set, complete order, and pairwise backbone. Each non-singleton level carries a two-
specification witness; each stable coarsening states what survived.
Three rules keep that output interpretable:
1. name (D, Fscope, q) and report primary and review-envelope conclusions separately;
2. give every STOP its missing object and minimum unblock, never a numeric surrogate; and
sections.content: 6 3. retain selection, exposure, and evidence license with the result. The machine-readable realization is deliberately appendix-facing; the main-text interface is the scoped claim, witness, and stable structure. 6 IMPLICATIONS, LIMITS, AND RELATED WORK

sections.title:
6.1
Evaluation releases should expose a claim-replay interface, not only task code and a headline metric.
For each advertised claim, the release should bind the historical observations or sufficient statistic,
evaluator/judge version, support and missingness decisions, typed aggregation, candidate family, and
query. The interface then either closes the claim or returns a typed stop naming what is missing.
This requirement is claim-relative rather than uniformly maximal. A direction may be recoverable
from a compact sufficient statistic, whereas exact-value replay can require sample-keyed outputs;
a winner can be identified even when the complete order is not. Reporting Iq(D, Fprimary) beside
Iq(D, Freview), together with witnesses and stable pairs, turns admission sensitivity into a reviewable
result. Appendix A.2 gives the expanded release design.
sections.content: Prospective utility remains an open test. This retrospective census diagnoses replay failures; it is not deployment trial of contract-compliant releases. It therefore does not estimate how many of the 110 stops new release process would prevent, or how often the added interface would change downstream decision. prospective test should register new release units and advertised claims before outcomes, require the claim-replay fields at release time, and compare replay completion, timeto-audit, and decision changes against the legacy interface. The observed stop codes and minimum unblocks define intervention targets and baseline denominator, not treatment effect.

sections.title:
6.3 RELATED WORK
Sensitivity analyses. Multiverse and specification-curve methods enumerate defensible analytic
choices (Steegen et al., 2016; Simonsohn et al., 2020; Silberzahn et al., 2018); benchmark work
likewise studies sensitivity to metrics, data, and protocols (Flach, 2019; Bouthillier et al., 2021;
Dehghani et al., 2021; D’Amour et al., 2022). Multicurious separates defensibility from equivalence
(Short et al., 2026), matching our distinction between why a candidate is live and whether it belongs to
the same-target family. These methods usually begin after an analyzable substrate and choice set have
been assembled. In this census, an available-case workflow would condition away 110 typed stops;
pooling all executable readings would also erase the AgentDojo/AutoML primary-versus-review
distinction, and a flip-only report would omit their stable winners and pairwise backbones. We
therefore add evidence-gate typing, admission-scoped families, and claim-resolution outputs before
and after enumeration; we do not claim a new general theory of sensitivity analysis.
sections.content: Partial identification. Set-valued identification, fine-to-coarse functionals, and the separation of identification from sampling precision are established (Tamer, 2010; Romano & Shaikh, 2008; Kasy, 2016). Robust ordinal regression similarly distinguishes necessary from possible preference relations (Greco et al., 2008), and label-uncertainty work bounds performance under ambiguous labels (Polo et al., 2024). We do not propose new general theory; we make these ideas executable for grounded evaluation families, including witnesses and stable pairwise backbone. Benchmark infrastructure and measurement. Evaluation frameworks organize tasks, scenarios, metrics, and execution (Liang et al., 2022; Kiela et al., 2021; Ribeiro et al., 2020), while audit work stresses documentation and the limits of aggregate leaderboards (Raji et al., 2021; Bowman & Dahl, 2021; Ethayarajh & Jurafsky, 2020). Measurement research separates constructs from operationalizations (Jacobs & Wallach, 2021; Bean et al., 2025; Salaudeen et al., 2025); judge 7 diagnostics study evaluator competence and spurious gains (Chen et al., 2026; Xu et al., 2026; Mahmud et al., 2026). Our contribution is the missing chain between these layers: finite-frame accounting evidential executability grounded family claim-level identified sets. Closest axes. Qin and Tong (2026) ask whether trajectories determine diagnostic object under fixed contract; Grynets et al. (2026) vary conforming implementations of one specification; FrameLevel AUC changes comparison populations while holding scores fixed (Abdulaziz & Bondarev, 2026). We connect commit-bound census accounting to grounded semantic families and claim-level identified sets.

sections.title:
6.4 CONCLUSION
Evaluation artifacts do not automatically license the claims attached to them. In the bound Inspect
Evals frame, the missing link is often the replay substrate or semantic registry needed to construct
(D, F, q). The proposed layer makes that absence explicit, and where execution closes it returns
scoped identified sets, witnesses, and stable structure. This is retrospective evidence for the diagnostic
interface, not yet evidence that adopting it prospectively will reduce stops or improve decisions. The
result is a reviewable claim-replay contract rather than a forced evaluator meaning or a single flip
label.

The row audit reconstructs 67/868 = 7.7189 pp; family collapse accounts for 61 of 67, or 91.0% in magnitude. 30 L.5 CROSS-CORPUS HETEROGENEITY AND UNCERTAINTY OBJECTS Under the baseline semantic design, AgentRx gives 2.40 pp with interval [5.82, 0] pp, TELBench gives 10.42 pp with [17.01, 4.86] pp, and the frozen interaction is +8.02 pp with [+1.47, +14.95] pp. The corpora are heterogeneous sources, not independent replications. An independent reconstruction rebuilt 220 raw observable/native-label records, 24,416 row scores, all denominators, margins, weak orders, and 10,000-draw bootstrap arrays; another rebuilt all 868 row-background records. Finite specification intervals vary declared semantics on fixed observations. Task-cluster intervals vary resampled tasks under one specification. Joint sign-pattern frequency is resampling statistic, not posterior ordering probability. possible-winner set is not complete-order identified set. Structural [0, 0] intervals hold only for the declared symmetric terminal family. None of these objects transports to unenumerated semantics without coverage or invariance assumption.
